subtitle: A request for reference materials on data communications and communications theory.

tldr.problem: The Center for Advanced Computation at the University of Illinois needed reference materials on data communications and communications theory to support their network research.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC author requests that each site's technical liaison send available references in the specified subject areas to a mailing address in Illinois.
tldr.outcome: This brief request demonstrates the collaborative nature of early network research and the importance of sharing reference materials across distributed sites.

today: RFC 81 is an Internet Experiment document. While brief and primarily administrative, it provides historical insight into how knowledge was shared among early ARPA network sites and the distributed, collaborative nature of network protocol development.

sections.title: The Reference Request
sections.content: RFC 81 is a brief administrative request from J. Bouknight at the Center for Advanced Computation (CAC) at the University of Illinois. The request asks technical liaison contacts at each site to send as many references as possible on two subject areas: data communications and communications theory.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asked other groups to send over reference materials they had about how networks work.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
This brief RFC reflects the collaborative, distributed nature of early ARPA network research. Different sites were implementing different protocols and systems, and sharing reference materials was part of the knowledge-sharing infrastructure that supported coordinated development. The CAC was preparing to join the network and needed background materials to support their implementation work.

Such requests were common during this period, as sites coordinated through both formal RFCs and informal communication channels to share technical knowledge and ensure that different implementations were informed by the same underlying theory and practice.
sections.plainLanguage: The different groups building the network shared knowledge and papers with each other so they would all understand the same ideas and build compatible systems.

sections.title: Contact Information
sections.content: The RFC provides a mailing address at the Center for Advanced Computation in Urbana, Illinois for sending the reference materials. This was typical of early network communication, where coordination happened through both the nascent network itself and traditional postal mail.
sections.plainLanguage: The request included an address where people should mail the materials they found.
